title: Anmol Ekka Double Fires India Into Fourth Straight Junior Asia Cup Final
excerpt: India beat Malaysia 3-1 in Moqi, China, with captain Ekka scoring twice and goalkeeper Vivek Lakra saving a penalty stroke; South Korea await in Sunday's final.
body:
• India beat Malaysia 3-1 in the semifinal of the AHF Junior Men's Asia Cup 2026 in Moqi, China, on Friday, reaching their fourth consecutive final.
  • Captain Anmol Ekka scored twice from penalty corners, taking his tournament tally to 16 goals and the top-scorer lead; Sukhvinder added the third.
  • Goalkeeper Vivek Lakra was named Player of the Match, saving a penalty stroke in the 53rd minute and holding firm through eight Malaysian penalty corners.
  • India will face South Korea in Sunday's final, with the defending champions bidding to retain the continental title.

India's junior men continued their march toward another continental crown on Friday, beating Malaysia 3-1 in the first semifinal of the AHF Junior Men's Asia Cup 2026 in Moqi, China, to reach their fourth consecutive final.

The defending champions, five-time winners of the tournament, found the breakthrough through captain and drag-flicker Anmol Ekka, whose second-half penalty-corner conversions proved decisive. Sukhvinder added India's third in a dominant display that also owed much to goalkeeper Vivek Lakra's heroics at the other end.

How the semifinal unfolded

The match remained scoreless through a tense first half, with Malaysia's defense holding firm against repeated Indian circle entries. India finally broke through after the break: following a Malaysian defensive touch that denied them in the 51st minute, the visitors immediately launched another circle entry and Sukhvinder finished the move to make it 2-0 — Anmol having opened the scoring earlier from the spot.

"The defending champions, five-time winners of the tournament, found the breakthrough through captain and drag-flicker Anmol Ekka, whose second-half penalty-corner conversions proved decisive."

Then came the defining sequence. Malaysia were awarded a penalty stroke in the 53rd minute, but Lakra dived sharply to his left and used his glove to keep the effort out. India turned defense into attack within a minute, earning a penalty corner in the 54th; Malaysia challenged through a video referral but lost it, and the PC stood. Anmol made no mistake, powering his flick straight past the goalkeeper to make it 3-0.

Malaysia earned a succession of penalty corners in the closing minutes — eight in all — but Lakra and the Indian defense stood firm. The goalkeeper produced another superb diving save from a well-struck flick in the 58th minute. Malaysia finally found a consolation goal through M. Rahuul with just 24 seconds remaining, off their eighth penalty corner.

Lakra's 53rd-minute stroke save and the failed video referral that kept India's 54th-minute penalty corner alive will be remembered as the moments the semifinal was won — defensive brilliance at one end, ruthless conversion at the other.

The road to the final

India have been the tournament's standout team. They finished top of Pool A with three wins and one draw, closing the group stage with a 15-0 demolition of Chinese Taipei in which Anmol scored six goals by himself. His semifinal double took his tournament tally to an impressive 16 goals, strengthening his position at the top of the scoring charts.

The Indian junior women's team has also reached a final, with Supriya's hat-trick sealing a 5-1 win over South Korea in the Junior Women's Asia Cup semifinal, per The Hindu.

Diaspora angle

For the diaspora, India's junior hockey pipeline matters as much as the senior team: it is where the next generation of stars emerges, and where tournaments like this one turn unknown teenagers into household names. Anmol Ekka's 16-goal campaign is already the kind of breakout that diaspora fans track closely — the junior circuit is Indian hockey's future, playing out in real time.

What's next

India face South Korea in Sunday's final (September 13) with the defending champions heavily favored but wary: Malaysia's late flurry of penalty corners showed how quickly a final can turn. A win would extend India's dominance of Asian junior hockey and send the squad — and its 16-goal captain — into the Junior World Cup cycle with serious momentum.
